local_bottleneck: Domestic CSOs require Ethiopian-national founders/members; a foreign founder can only register a foreign NGO office, which needs a local entity and CSO Agency approval.
deduction: Charitable gifts deductible up to 10% of taxable income (Ethiopian residents); CSOs exempt on grants/dues.
foreign_donor_restriction: 2021 reform allows foreign funding of registered CSOs, but funds must flow through the CSO Agency/ACSO channel; no direct foreign donor license.
corrections: Confirm prior: 2021 CSO Proclamation (1259/2021) keeps foreign founders out of domestic entities; cost 3-6 months via partner is reasonable.

local_bottleneck: No functioning independent civil society; all associations are state-controlled and donor funds must pass through government ministries.
deduction: No practical charitable deduction regime; tax system minimal and not applied to charitable giving.
foreign_donor_restriction: All NGO funding must be channeled through Eritrean government ministries (NGO Proclamation 145/2005); de facto ban on independent foreign charity work.
corrections: Confirm prior: no legal pathway for an independent foreign-founded charity; state control confirmed by 2005 NGO Proclamation.

local_bottleneck: Associations must be registered with the Ministry of Interior with a local office and Djiboutian leadership; security-driven discretion makes remote foreign founding impractical.
deduction: Charitable gifts to registered associations can be deducted for resident taxpayers under the personal income tax code (modest regime).
foreign_donor_restriction: Foreign funding of associations is subject to approval/supervision; no explicit FCRA-style register, but aid actors register through local partners.
corrections: Confirm prior: association law requires local involvement; cost ~$100-300 and 1-3 months plausible.

local_bottleneck: Fragmented federal state: separate regional NGO laws (Puntland, South West, etc.); foreign NGOs register regionally with local offices, security plan, and embassy channel.
deduction: No developed charitable deduction regime; limited/no formal tax incentives for donations.
foreign_donor_restriction: Foreign NGOs need regional government registration and approval of staff; no FCRA-style donor licensing, but registration itself is the gate.
corrections: Confirm prior: severe insecurity and fragmented registries; domestic charities need Somali founders; 3-6 months is optimistic, extend to 12.

local_bottleneck: De facto state: requires local registration with the Planning/Interior ministry and local office; banking and sanctions compliance add friction for a remote founder.
deduction: No formal charitable tax-deduction regime in practice.
foreign_donor_restriction: NGOs Law (2010) and I NGO Law regulate foreign NGOs; foreign groups face scrutiny over acting as implementers, but no donor ban.
corrections: Confirm prior: 2010 NGO law (not 2005) governs; registry is relatively functional; cost 1-3 months plausible.

local_bottleneck: Foreign NGOs register through the embassy channel with a local office and South Sudanese staff (proposed 80% local staffing); security and weak institutions slow everything.
deduction: Charitable deductions exist in the Income Tax Act for registered donors but are rarely used; no formal public charitable-giving incentive.
foreign_donor_restriction: NGO Act 2016 requires registration, local office, and approval of funding; no FCRA-style donor register, registration is the gate.
corrections: Confirm prior, update: governing law is NGO Act 2016 (not 2009); 2023 amendment bill adds 80% local staff requirement; 6-12 months realistic.

local_bottleneck: Requires a licensed local agent and registered office in Seychelles; founders/directors can be 100% foreign, so remote setup is routine for a fee.
deduction: No domestic charitable deduction regime for offshore foundations; Seychelles foundations are generally tax-neutral, not tax-privileged donors.
foreign_donor_restriction: No restrictions on foreign donors; foundations receive no special public-benefit status without local activity.
corrections: Confirm prior: NPO Act 2013 for local NPOs; the practical foreign route is the Seychelles Foundation Act 2009 (SIBA, $200 gov fee); prior $1,500-3,000 is agent-inclusive.

local_bottleneck: Needs a registered office and local registered agent in Mauritius; foreign founders/directors fully permitted, so remote setup is straightforward.
deduction: Donations to approved public-benefit NPOs/donate trusts are deductible by resident donors; offshore foundations get no local public-benefit status.
foreign_donor_restriction: No restrictions on foreign donors; the IFSA foundation route (Foundations Act 2012) is explicitly open to foreign founders with non-resident beneficiaries.
corrections: Confirm prior: Foundations Act is 2012 (not 2014); NPO Act 2003 remains for local NPOs; $500-1,500 prior is agent-inclusive, gov fees are far lower.
